title: Judge validity vs human judgment — SummEval, system level (the aggregation most published numbers use)
what_this_is: The SAME data and scorers as the pooled summary-level card, re-aggregated per system (n=16 systems). This is the aggregation level at which most published '0.6-class' meta-evaluation numbers (e.g. the UFAL/RWS r ~ 0.63 often cited alongside ours) live. Publishing both cards makes the aggregation effect explicit instead of letting either number masquerade as THE number.
aggregation_note: Mean proxy loss vs mean human loss per system, n=16 systems; validity confirmed by permutation test.

results.scorer: range across scorers and axes (see provenance)

provenance.documented_in: docs/PROOF_BOUNDARY.md (calibration scope section: 'system-level (n=16 systems; validity confirmed by permutation test) correlations are rho/r ~ 0.57-0.75')

scope_limits: n=16 systems is small; the bootstrap CI on the headline (0.70 [0.49, 0.83]) is wide.
System-level validity means the proxy ranks SYSTEMS sensibly; it does not upgrade the per-summary (pooled) validity of ~0.27-0.33.
Do not quote the 0.57-0.75 range without naming the aggregation level; that omission is exactly the overclaim-by-omission this card family exists to prevent.
reading_guidance: Cite this card when comparing SUM's proxy to published system-level meta-evaluation numbers; cite the pooled card when the question is per-document trustworthiness.
